profile.headline: Artificial Intelligence Research Scientist
profile.summary:
As an Artificial Intelligence Research Scientist, I have explored a range of advanced algorithms across the Deep Learning spectrum. My experience includes working with ResNet, ConvNeXt, and SWIN for real-time video classification, PointNet, PointNet++, Point Cloud Transformer, and Point Transformer for 3D mesh regression, and BERT, MISTRAL, and LLAMA for uncertainty-aware retrieval-augmented generation. This diverse expertise highlights my ability to tackle complex AI challenges.

I hold a Master’s in Data Science and Data Engineering, along with dual Bachelor’s degrees in Applied Mathematics and Computer Science, all Summa Cum Laude. My undergraduate honors include the Department of Mathematics and Statistics Outstanding Junior Award and the Dean's Medalist distinction. This solid academic foundation has supported my transition from software development to data science, merging theoretical knowledge with practical skills. With 3 years of combined experience in software development and AI, including roles in various Agile environments, I bring a well-rounded skill set. My background includes collaborating effectively with both small and large teams, iterating quickly, and delivering impactful results.

My data science journey began with a project simulating college football commitments, achieving over 50% accuracy in predicting student-athlete choices among 100+ universities. In collaboration with Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, I led a project on electrocardiogram classification, reaching over 99% accuracy and improving model interpretability. I also developed an innovative uncertainty-aware dynamic thresholding method for time series classification for a Parsons-funded project. Most recently, at Corvid Technologies, I adapted PointNet and PointNet++ for regression tasks involving cloud-level metadata.

Specializing in uncertainty-aware autonomous decision-making, I am dedicated to uncovering insights within data. By combining statistical expertise with practical data engineering skills, I aim to provide not only accurate models but also transparent and understandable AI solutions, empowering users to confidently rely on and interpret the insights driving their decisions.

positions.title: Project Lead
positions.description:
Senior Design Project for Master of Science in Data Science and Data Engineering at Auburn University, working for Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory.

Compared uncertainty estimation for NumPy and PyTorch Python implementations of a robust Gaussian Process approach (MuyGPs) versus Random Forest Variants, K Nearest Neighbors, and a Convolutional Neural Network.

Led a 3-person team in the completion of this project using BinaryEdge’s Data Science Workflow.

Converted Marine Predator Algorithm from MATLAB to Python and adapted it to hyperparameter tuning.

projects.title: Uncertainty-Aware Coordinate Driven Missile Classification
projects.description: Generating rapid and reliable information about unguided missile flyouts immediately upon detection is crucial for effective defense systems. We propose a method to quickly classify missiles in flight into predefined groupings based on their physical characteristics, inferred solely from their movement in the X and Z axes over time. Previous work on this problem has achieved results within 15 seconds of launch or extremely high accuracy, but not both simultaneously. We introduce CRUD: Coordinate-Driven, Robust, & Uncertainty-Aware Dynamic Missile Classification, an approach that enhances dataset robustness and employs uncertainty-aware machine learning. Our dataset consists of positional data from simulated missile flyouts. To improve generalizability, the dataset is augmented to include varied detection times, frequency irregularities, Gaussian noise, and data gaps. We derive velocities and accelerations from the positional data and combine them with their magnitudes, creating a comprehensive feature set for each time step, which is then summarized into statistical metrics for the classification pipeline. Our pipeline evaluates a Neural Network, a Gradient-Boosted Classifier, and a Random Forest, aiming for early-stage classification and using the maximum margin of their probability space for uncertainty. Reliability is enhanced through random state ensembling. We calculate the Z-Score required for the confidence interval to include 0, indicating equal probabilities for all classes and complete ambiguity. Results indicate that our framework achieves high classification accuracy early in flight. The Random Forest model excels, boasting >99.9% accuracy and rapid classification times under two seconds on average. This framework significantly boosts early classification accuracy and reliability, providing a powerful tool for defense systems requiring rapid and precise missile identification.
